tayla: Customer ACME reported a sudden p99 jump (10s -> 1.8s) right after yesterday's microbatching rollout. They see most slow traces on short prompts (~30-60 tokens).
omar: can you paste the tenant id + sample request?
tayla: tenant=acme-corp, sample curl below. Also sending span ids in thread.
tayla: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -d '{"input": "Hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
lee: :eyes: logs show a bunch of `batch_wait` events where tiny requests wait for `grace_window` and then explode when batch fills. Also a handful of 401s from auth refresh failures mixed in.
lee: snippet from runner logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] req=abc batch_wait hold_ms=40 size=1
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] req=def auth_refresh failed, status=401 tenant=acme-corp
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] req=ghi batch_send size=16 latency=120ms
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] req=abc tail_latency=1840ms
```
alice: support notes: customer said this was intermittent and maps to their SDK calling `refresh()` on every request (old client), so auth flapping likely serialized their small requests.
omar: that matches. Continuous batcher is sensitive: tiny prompts + auth errors -> requests stick in hold window and then flush in one big batch. p99 gets dominated by the stuck ones.
tayla: reproduction steps I used: run locust with 200 rps of 30-token prompts from single tenant, enable mode `continuous` with config below. Repro consistent in ~2m.
tayla: ```json
{
  "batcher": {
    "mode": "continuous",
    "max_batch_size": 32,
    "hold_ms": 40,
    "grace_ms": 8
  },
  "auth": {
    "refresh_window_ms": 0
  }
}
```
lee: repro note: when I injected 5% 401s (simulating auth jitter) p99 jumped above 1.5s. Without 401s p99 ~200ms.
omar: potential mitigations: 1) short-term feature-flag to route tenant to `unbatched` path 2) increase `hold_ms` to reduce flush amplification 3) make auth failures bypass batching queue (fast-fail) 4) teach batcher to cap per-req wait if upstream auth pending.
lee: quick mitigation I can push: a tenant-level override to set `batcher.mode=single` for acme-corp. That avoids batching amplification.
alice: customer ok with short downtime for quick fix.
omar: can someone confirm the config path and a one-line change? I can roll a hotpatch if we agree.
lee: config key is `tenants.acme-corp.features.batching_mode`. change from `continuous` -> `single`.
tayla: I'll get ACME on standby.
lee: I'm going to upload a small canary: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runner BATCHING_MODE=single --overwrite` on a single node pool for the tenant routing. Will monitor traces.
omar: also let's add a defensive server-side change: if a request sees auth error during preflight, mark it as `auth_failed` and immediately bypass coalesce queue; i'll open a tiny PR for that.
lee: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1245 (draft) — implements fast-fail bypass + counter metric `batcher.bypassed.auth`
tayla: after routing ACME to `single`, their p99 dropped to 210ms within 3 minutes. Customer confirmed improved. :thumbsup:
omar: follow-ups: 1) rollback not needed; leave single-mode while we ship auth-bypass. 2) add a telemetry alert for `batcher.bypassed.auth` rate>0.5% per tenant. 3) advise SDK team to rate-limit refresh calls (client-side fix).
alee: (typo) actually lee: add unit tests for race between auth events and coalesce flush.
omar: assigning: lee -> canary prod change + metric, tayla -> coordinate ACME, devex -> post short client FAQ, eng-sre -> watch cluster p99.
lee: starting canary now. deploy-bot: rollout started for runner pool `tenant-acme` :rocket:
pagerbot: alert muted for tenant acme during canary window.
tayla: closing loop with customer, will create support-ticket with repro steps + request they upgrade SDK to 0.12.3 which has `refresh` debounce.
omar: thanks team. I'll keep PR moving and follow up in this thread.
